<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Ioánnem
<r>Ioannes 7:1-13</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Ambulábat Iesus in Galilǽam: non enim volébat in Iudǽam ambuláre, quia quærébant eum Iudǽi interfícere. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
<r>Tractatus 28 in Ioannem</r>
<c>I</c>n isto Evangélii capítulo, fratres, Dóminus noster Iesus Christus secúndum hóminem se plúrimum commendávit fídei nostræ. Etenim semper hoc egit dictis et factis suis, ut Deus credátur et homo: Deus qui nos fecit, homo qui nos quæsívit: Deus cum Patre semper, homo nobíscum ex témpore. Non enim quǽreret quem fécerat, nisi fíeret ipse quod fécerat. Verum hoc mementóte, et de córdibus vestris nolíte dimíttere: sic esse Christum hóminem factum, ut non destíterit Deus esse.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus meus es tu, ne discédas a me:
* Quóniam tribulátio próxima est, et non est qui ádiuvet.
<r>℣.</r> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam tribulátio próxima est, et non est qui ádiuvet.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to John
<r>John 7:1-13</r>
<c>A</c>t that time: Jesus walked in Galilee; for he would not walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him. And so on.

Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop <n>of Hippo.</n>
<r>28th Tract on John</r>
<c>I</c>n this chapter of the Gospel, my brethren, our Lord Jesus Christ hath much commended Himself unto our faith, as touching His Manhood. At the same time, His words and works were alway such as to give us to believe that He is both God and Man, yea, that God Who made us, and that Man Who hath sought us, yea, God the Son, Who, as touching His Godhead, is alway with the Father, <n>John i. 18; iii. 13,</n> and, as touching His Manhood, hath been with us in time. <n>Matth. i. 23.</n> For He had not sought the work of His hands unless He had been made His own work. <n>John i. 14.</n> Keep this well in mind, and let your hearts never forget it, namely, that Christ was not made Man so as to cease to be God.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Thou art my God; be not far from me, for trouble is near;
* For there is none to help.
<r>℣.</r> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me.
<r>℟.</r> For trouble is near; for there is none to help.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>M</c>anens Deus accépit hóminem, qui fecit hóminem. Quando ergo látuit ut homo, non poténtiam perdidísse putándus est, sed exémplum infirmitáti præbuísse. Ille enim quando vóluit, deténtus est: quando vóluit, occísus est. Sed quóniam futúra erant membra eius, id est, fidéles eius, qui non habérent illam potestátem, quam habébat ipse Deus noster: quod latébat, quod se tamquam ne occiderétur, occultábat, hoc indicábat factúra esse membra sua, in quibus útique membris suis ipse erat.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Tota die contristátus ingrediébar, Dómine: quóniam ánima mea compléta est illusiónibus:
* Et vim faciébant, qui quærébant ánimam meam.
<r>℣.</r> Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: et dolos tota die meditabántur.
<r>℟.</r> Et vim faciébant, qui quærébant ánimam meam.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>H</c>e, Who made the Manhood, took It into that Godhead Which is His from everlasting to everlasting. While therefore He lay hid in the Manhood, we must not think that He had suffered any lessening of power, but that He was giving example to our weakness. When He willed it, He was taken; when He willed it, He was put to death. <n>John x. 18.</n> But, since He was to have members, that is, His faithful people, who would not have that power over their lives which He, our God, had over His, He hid Himself, He concealed Himself, as if it were to escape being put to death, to show what should be done by those His members in whom He should dwell.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O Lord, I go mourning all the day long, for my soul is filled with a loathsome disease
* They also that sought after my life have used violence against me.

<r>℟.</r> They also that sought after my life have used violence against me.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>N</c>on enim Christus in cápite, et non in córpore: sed Christus totus in cápite, et in córpore. Quod ergo membra eius, ipse: quod autem ipse, non contínuo membra eius. Nam si non ipsi essent membra eius, non díceret Saulo: Quid me perséqueris? Non enim Saulus ipsum, sed membra eius, id est, fidéles eius, in terra persequebátur. Nóluit tamen dícere sanctos meos, servos meos, postrémo honorabílius, fratres meos: sed me, hoc est membra mea, quibus ego sum caput.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris: et de manu contra legem agéntis, et iníqui:
* Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea.
<r>℣.</r> Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus. et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea.
<n>Gloria omittitur</n>
<r>℟.</r> Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris: et de manu contra legem agéntis, et iníqui: * Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>hrist is not the Head of His Church in such sense that He is not in her Body; but the whole Christ is in the Head, and the whole Christ is in the Body. That, then, which His members are is Himself, though That Which He is, That are not therefore His members. For if His members had not been indeed His Own, how had He said unto Saul, <n>Acts ix. 4</n>: Why persecutest thou Me? since Saul was not persecuting Him in Himself, but in His members, that is, in His faithful ones which were upon earth. He said not: Why persecutest thou My holy ones, nor: My servants, no, nor yet called He them by that more honourable name “My brethren”, but, “Why persecutest thou Me?”; that is, the members of My Body, whose Head I am.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, and out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
* For Thou art my hope.
<r>℣.</r> Deliver me from my enemies, O my God. and defend me from them that rise up against me.
<r>℟.</r> For Thou art my hope.

b.ba26423375:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>extodécimo Kaléndas Aprílis Luna nona. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>pud civitátem Dunum, in Hibérnia, natális sancti Patrícii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui primus in ea ínsula Christum evangelizávit, et máximis miráculis et virtútibus cláruit.
<h>H</h>ierosólymis sancti Ioseph ab Arimathǽa, qui nóbilis Decúrio et discípulus Dómini éxstitit; atque ipsíus Dómini corpus, de cruce depósitum, in monuménto suo novo sepelívit.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctórum Alexándri et Theodóri Mártyrum.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui a Serápidis cultóribus comprehénsi, et, cum adoráre idólum constánter renuíssent, sævíssime cæsi sunt, témpore Theodósii Imperatóris; qui mox rescríptum dedit, ut Serápidis templum destruerétur.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Pauli Mártyris, qui, sub Constantíno Coprónymo, cum sanctárum Imáginum cultum defénderet, igne combústus est.
<h>C</h>abillóne, in Gálliis, sancti Agrícolæ Epíscopi.
<h>N</h>ivigéllæ, in Brabántia, sanctæ Gertrúdis Vírginis, quæ, claríssimo génere orta, despíciens mundum et toto vitæ suæ cursu in ómnibus sanctitátis offíciis se exércens, Christum sponsum in cælis habére méruit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.6d3401749a:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>arch 17th 2027, the 9th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Ireland, the holy Confessor Patrick, Bishop [of Armagh,] the first who there preached the Gospel of Christ, and who was famous for great miracles and works of power, [in the year 464.]
<h>A</h>t Jerusalem, holy Joseph of Arimathea, the honourable councillor, the disciple of the Lord, who took down His Body from the cross and laid it in his own new tomb.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander and Theodore.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria are commemorated many holy martyrs, who were seized by the worshippers of Serapis, and because they would not worship that idol were cruelly murdered by them, in the time of the Emperor Theodosius, who presently afterward sent a rescript to destroy the temple of Serapis.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy martyr Paul, who was burnt under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus for defending the honouring of holy images.
<h>A</h>t Chalons [-sur-Saône,] in Gaul, holy Agricola, Bishop of that see, [in the year 580.]
<h>A</h>t Nivelles, in Brabant, the holy Virgin Gertrude, the daughter of an illustrious race, who despised this world, and busied herself all her life in holy deeds, so that she won to be espoused to Christ in heaven, [in the year 659.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
